speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a newborn, I will be asking your parents about your symptoms and history. Can you describe what brought you to see us today and when the symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the background. I see the infant is a term female with no prenatal care or immunization history. Does she have any specific physical findings, such as jaundice, feeding difficulties, or respiratory distress?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome. The clinical triad of cataracts (cloudy lenses), sensorineural hearing loss (auditory failure), and a characteristic heart murmur (patent ductus arteriosus), combined with non-blanching blue macules (purpura), confirms this diagnosis.
